draft.change: Link the existing Abram article to אבה through its father element and add Genesis 12:4 as an example.
draft.definition: Abram, son of Terah, later named Abraham. The name means “exalted father.”
draft.evidence: Genesis 12:4 repeats the name אַבְרָם when giving Abram’s age at departure. The name’s אָב element belongs to Haqor’s אבה article.

analysis.evidence: אַבְרָם is the subject of יָשַׁב. The verse contrasts where Abram settled, in the land of Canaan, with where Lot settled, in the cities of the plain.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Abram, the son of Terah later named Abraham

analysis.evidence: בְּאֶרֶץ כְּנָעַן identifies where Abram lived. The parallel clause uses the same verb to describe where Lot lived after the two separated.
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, third person masculine singular, agreeing with אַבְרָם.
analysis.sense: to dwell habitually in a place

analysis.evidence: אַבְרָם יָשַׁב בְּאֶרֶץ כְּנָעַן means “Abram lived in the land of Canaan.” The place name כְּנָעַן identifies the territory where Abram lived.
analysis.morphology: The preposition בְּ means “in.” The common-gender noun אֶרֶץ is singular and stands in construct before כְּנָעַן.

analysis.evidence: In אַבְרָם יָשַׁב בְּאֶרֶץ כְּנָעַן, “Abram lived in the land of Canaan,” כְּנָעַן follows the construct noun אֶרֶץ and names the territory where Abram lived.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun. The initial כ is part of the name. The word has no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: The parallel clauses אַבְרָם יָשַׁב and וְלוֹט יָשַׁב name Abram and Lot as the subjects of the same verb. Abram settled in Canaan, and Lot settled in the cities of the plain.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וְ is prefixed to the masculine personal name לוֹט.

analysis.evidence: The parallel clauses identify where Abram and Lot settled. With Lot as subject, בְּעָרֵי הַכִּכָּר places his residence among the cities of the plain, and the next clause says he pitched his tent as far as Sodom.
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, third person masculine singular, with Lot as its subject.
analysis.sense: to take up residence in a place

draft.change: Add Genesis 13:12 as evidence for the existing city sense of עִיר in article 3yr.
draft.definition: A city or town, here one of the settlements of the plain.
draft.evidence: Genesis 13:12 uses the plural construct עָרֵי in the phrase identifying where Lot lived.

analysis.evidence: The two clauses use יָשַׁב to say where each man lived. Abram lived בְּאֶרֶץ כְּנָעַן, “in the land of Canaan,” and Lot lived בְּעָרֵי הַכִּכָּר, “in the cities of the plain.” The reference to Sodom locates Lot among those settlements.
analysis.morphology: The locative preposition בְּ precedes עָרֵי, the feminine plural construct of עִיר. The following definite noun הַכִּכָּר makes the whole phrase definite.

draft.change: Add the geographic sense of כִּכָּר under כרר and correct the occurrence gloss to “plain.”
draft.definition: The plain along a river, here the plain of the Jordan.
draft.evidence: Genesis 13:10 identifies the Jordan as the river and describes the land Lot sees along it as well watered.

analysis.evidence: בְּעָרֵי הַכִּכָּר means “in the cities of the plain.” The article points back to the Jordan plain named in Genesis 13:10, and the mention of Sodom locates Lot within that district.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הַ precedes a singular absolute noun of common gender. The article accounts for the dagesh in the initial כ.
analysis.sense: A plain or district along a river.

analysis.evidence: After saying that Lot lived in the cities of the plain, the verse adds וַיֶּאֱהַל עַד סְדֹם. The phrase עַד סְדֹם gives the extent of Lot’s encampment, “as far as Sodom.”
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וַ introduces a Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with Lot as its subject.

analysis.evidence: In וַיֶּאֱהַל עַד סְדֹם, Sodom marks the limit of Lot’s tent-pitching. He pitched his tents as far as Sodom.
analysis.morphology: A preposition with no prefix or suffix. Its complement is the place name סְדֹם.
analysis.sense: as far as, up to, to (a place or person)

draft.change: Add a standalone place-name article for סְדֹם, keyed by its own consonants סדמ. The supplied root סגר does not account for this form.
draft.definition: סְדֹם is the Hebrew name of the city of Sodom.
draft.evidence: Genesis 10:19 names Sodom alongside Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboiim in its description of Canaanite territory.

analysis.evidence: In וַיֶּאֱהַל עַד סְדֹם, “he pitched his tents as far as Sodom,” עַד introduces the place marking the extent of Lot’s encampment.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun with no prefix or suffix.
